newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore dollar hits 17-mth low on ringgit buying.
newsitem.headline: Singapore dollar hits 17-mth low on ringgit buying.

text.p: The Singapore dollar hit a 17-month low against the U.S. dollar on Friday as U.S. investment banks and hedge funds sold the currency against the U.S. unit and the Malaysian ringgit, dealers said.
The Singapore dollar was quoted at 1.4320/30 to the U.S. unit in late trade after reaching a low of 1.4340 for the first time since October 3, 1995.
"People are still trying to buy the ringgit/Sing today. And we heard there was good (U.S. dollar) buying interest at 1.4300 from oil companies in Brunei," said a U.S. bank dealer.

Traders said U.S. hedge funds were going into the ringgit/Sing cross for its yield and Malaysia's strong economic fundamentals. The cross was quoted at 0.5774/81 after hitting a high of 0.5785 earlier.
The ringgit received a slight boost earlier in the day after Malaysian Finance Minister Anwar Ibrahim said he saw no immediate need to lower interest rates to spur the economy.
A Japanese bank dealer said U.S. investment banks had been active buyers of dollar/Sing after it breached the 1.4300 barrier overnight.
"Dollar/Sing has broken 1.4300 after a long time. Maybe they're bullish the dollar/Sing now," he said, adding that an estimated $500 million had probably been traded.
The U.S. bank dealer said the U.S. dollar had come up against selling pressure from a range of sources above the 1.4240 level.
"We've seen some U.K. clearing banks offering there from London and some local companies also," he said.
"I think it'll probably trade in a 1.4300/40 range for now but it'll eventually go higher. The next target would be 1.4500, though that could be the target for the year," he added.
